result:
I looked at the spreadsheet you described: Seed, Packets, Borrower, Date out, Date back. About a third of the Date back cells are empty. That gap could mean very different things. Some of those seeds may truly be still out. Some may have come back without anyone writing it down. And at many seed libraries, borrowers aren't expected to return the same packets at all, but to bring back seed they saved from their own plants next season. Each of those leads to a different tool: a reminder system, an easier check-in, or something that tracks harvests and seasons rather than loans.

When you look at those empty Date back cells, what do you think is really behind most of them, and what problem is that causing for the garden?
